description: Replay the Chapter 274 Random Schedule policy using supplied priority words.

source.title: Packet Switching in Multi-queue Switches
source.algorithm_attribution: Random Schedule; procedural steps pinned to Albers and Jacobs §3.2

input.encoding: [queue_count, queue_capacity, slot_count, arrival_flags[m*T] slot-major, priority_words[m*T] slot-major]

workspace.meaning: Bounded queue loads, auxiliary priority tags and mark bits, and staged output.

contract.arrival_phase: Each 0/1 flag is one possible packet arrival. Admit it only if its data queue has space; reject arrivals to full queues. On admission, append the matching priority word as an unmarked tag, evicting the oldest tag first if the auxiliary queue already has capacity B.
contract.priority_mapping: For an admitted packet, integer word r in 0..2^32-1 represents (r+1)/(2^32+1), a value strictly between 0 and 1. Words for absent or rejected arrivals are ignored.
contract.service_phase: Choose the largest unmarked tag across auxiliary queues, mark it, and serve its queue. When no unmarked tag exists, serve the smallest-index nonempty queue. Record -1 if all queues are empty.
contract.ties: Equal priorities choose the smallest queue index, then the oldest tag in that queue; this fixes choices that the source leaves arbitrary.
contract.error_results: Malformed input returns -1. Null output or capacity below 8*slot_count returns -2 without writes.
contract.scope: The priority tape makes this trace deterministic. It does not generate random values or claim the source's probabilistic competitive guarantee.

oracle_method: The primary reference simulates per-queue priority-tag lists; the independent reference uses serial-numbered event records and a canonical global ordering.
